name: Bokar-Ramo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ouyang, Jueya. 1985. Luobazu yuyan jianzhi (Bengni-Boga'eryu) [Sketch grammar of Bengni-Bokar]. Beijing: Minzu Chubanshe — sketch grammar with phonology; not readable online.

sources.note: No descriptive refs attached to boka1249 itself; the justification note cites Megu 1990, Grewal 1997, Ouyang 1985 and Sun 1993 ('Bokar.. far too divergent'). Dialects listed include Pailibo (pail1243) and Ramo.

sources.citation: Grambank v1 CLDF (local copy, boka1249 rows.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grambank has no word-stress feature; the sheet cites 'Ouyang 1985: in passim' (s_Ouyang_Luoba), confirming Ouyang 1985 as the the deciding source for this lect.

sources.citation: Ete, Geyi. 2017. A Descriptive Study of Bokar Language. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Deccan College Post Graduate & Research Institute, Pune (supervisor Shailendra Mohan). 284 pp. Shodhganga handle 10603/560235 (deposited 2024; Glottolog ref 571106 dates it 2019).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent anywhere in the thesis (all chapters a full-text search for stress/accent; the only hits, 'long stress' ch. 3 pp. 94-96, mean vowel lengthening in demonstratives si/si:, a/a:, ta/ta:, ba/ba:). Ch. 2 §2.2 p. 41: 'Bokar is not a tonal language and intonation does not play a role for identifying phonemes.' §2.16 Tone pp. 74-75 and p. 187: no tone system found. Describes the Karm/Hill dialect, Monigong area (Pujen village), West Siang.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Bokar language', revision downloaded 2026-09-17 (phonology section citing Sun 1993: 495, Ouyang 1985, Megu 1990).
sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables only; no mention of stress or tone.

sources.note: The primary national-academy sketch of Bokar (Nanyi, Mainling), the source Glottolog, Grambank and Sun 1993 all rest on; the 简志 series' 语音 chapter is where a statement on 重音 (stress) and 声调 (tone) for Bokar would be found. Named by the earlier scan as the source; still unreachable.

sources.note: Modern family overview by the two leading Tani specialists; would give the Tani-wide prosodic type (tone absent; stress/prominence) that applies to Bokar, and cites the current Bokar/Ramo fieldwork.

sources.citation: Sun, Tianshin Jackson. 1993. A historical-comparative study of the Tani (Mirish) branch in Tibeto-Burman. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.

sources.note: Contains synchronic phonological summaries of Tani lects including Bokar (from Ouyang's Chinese data) and Tani-wide remarks on prosody; the most authoritative comparative treatment and the one most likely to state whether Tani/Bokar has word stress.

sources.note: Only other Arunachal-side description of Bokar (Glottolog's justification source); a practical language guide that Ete 2017 rates as phonologically poor, so low chance of a usable stress statement, but it is the cited the deciding source and HathiTrust search-only could confirm whether 'stress' appears.
